status_source.name: Indigenous Watchdog
status_source.note: Third-party classifications, not TRC Tracker findings.

calls.title: Reduce Indigenous children in care
calls.responsible: Federal, provincial, territorial and Indigenous governments
requirements: Monitor and assess neglect investigations.
Resource Indigenous communities and child-welfare organizations to keep families together safely.
Ensure culturally appropriate environments for children.
Train child-welfare decision-makers on residential school history and impacts.
Require decision-makers to consider the impacts of residential schools.
calls.hard_truth: A child-welfare law is not the same as a demonstrated reduction in Indigenous children entering care.

calls.title: Publish child welfare data
calls.responsible: Federal government, in collaboration with Indigenous organizations
requirements: Publish annual reports on the number of Indigenous children in care.
Compare reasons for apprehension, prevention spending, and effectiveness of interventions.
Track progress toward reducing the number of children in care.
calls.hard_truth: Without consistent annual public data, Canadians cannot independently test whether child-welfare reforms are working.

calls.title: Implement Jordan’s Principle
requirements: Fully implement Jordan’s Principle so First Nations children can access needed public services without jurisdictional delays.
calls.hard_truth: Jordan’s Principle is about timely access to services, not simply announcing a funding envelope.

calls.title: Establish Indigenous child welfare standards
requirements: Enact Indigenous child-welfare legislation establishing national standards.
Affirm Indigenous governments’ right to maintain their own child-welfare agencies.
Require adequate resources and culturally appropriate practices.
calls.hard_truth: Legislation alone cannot demonstrate that Indigenous child-welfare systems have sufficient resources and authority.

calls.title: Develop culturally appropriate parenting programs
calls.responsible: Federal, provincial, territorial and Indigenous governments
requirements: Develop culturally appropriate parenting programs for Indigenous families.
calls.hard_truth: A culturally appropriate parenting program must be accessible to families, not merely described in policy.

calls.title: Repeal section 43 of the Criminal Code
calls.hard_truth: The TRC explicitly called for repeal of Criminal Code section 43; discussion of reform is not repeal.

calls.title: Eliminate educational and employment gaps
calls.hard_truth: Education and employment gaps require measured outcomes, not just program announcements.

calls.title: Improve Indigenous education outcomes
calls.hard_truth: Comparable per-student funding matters; an announced investment does not automatically close a funding gap.

calls.title: Report on First Nations education funding
calls.hard_truth: Without transparent education funding and outcome data, accountability remains difficult.

calls.title: Develop culturally appropriate education agreements
calls.hard_truth: A commitment to new education legislation is not the same as meeting every TRC principle for its development.

calls.title: Fund First Nations post-secondary education
calls.hard_truth: Post-secondary access depends on sustained funding and actual student opportunity.

calls.title: Create Indigenous early childhood programs
calls.hard_truth: Early childhood programs need culturally appropriate delivery and dependable access.

calls.title: Recognize Indigenous language rights
requirements: Acknowledge that Aboriginal rights include Aboriginal language rights.
calls.hard_truth: Recognizing language rights is an important step, but language survival depends on sustained revitalization.

calls.title: Enact Indigenous languages legislation
requirements: Enact an Aboriginal Languages Act with Indigenous peoples.
Recognize urgency of language preservation and revitalization.
Provide sufficient funding for language revitalization and preservation.
calls.hard_truth: The Indigenous Languages Act exists; the hard question is whether its principles are fully funded and realized.

calls.title: Appoint an Indigenous languages commissioner
requirements: Appoint an Aboriginal Languages Commissioner in consultation with Aboriginal groups.
calls.hard_truth: Creating an office is not the same as ensuring language revitalization succeeds.

calls.title: Fund Indigenous language post-secondary programs
calls.hard_truth: A degree program alone cannot replace community-led language transmission.

calls.title: Restore names changed by residential schools
calls.hard_truth: Reclaiming an Indigenous name should not be blocked by avoidable administrative cost.

calls.title: Recognize Indigenous health rights
calls.hard_truth: Acknowledging Indigenous health rights does not by itself close health disparities.

calls.title: Close Indigenous health outcome gaps
calls.hard_truth: Without published, comparable health outcomes, promises to close gaps cannot be fully evaluated.

calls.title: Address Indigenous health jurisdiction
calls.hard_truth: Jurisdictional disputes should not prevent Indigenous peoples from receiving care.

calls.title: Fund Indigenous healing centres
calls.hard_truth: A healing-centre funding announcement is not proof that communities have sufficient long-term services.

calls.title: Recognize value of Indigenous healing practices
calls.hard_truth: Respect for Indigenous healing practices must be meaningful in care, not merely ceremonial.

calls.title: Increase Indigenous health professionals
calls.hard_truth: Recruitment goals need actual Indigenous health workforce outcomes.

calls.title: Provide cultural competency training in health care
calls.hard_truth: Cultural competency training must change practice, not just attendance records.

calls.title: Affirm Aboriginal rights in legal policy
calls.hard_truth: Police independence must be protected when governments have interests in related litigation.

calls.title: Review limitation periods in historical abuse cases
calls.hard_truth: Fair access to justice requires addressing barriers in historic abuse claims.

calls.title: Ensure legal independence for abuse claims
calls.hard_truth: Legal education about Indigenous peoples should be substantive and accountable.

calls.title: Require law students to study Indigenous legal history and rights
calls.hard_truth: Law-school curriculum commitments need consistent implementation and evaluation.

calls.title: Resolve legal issues involving residential school claims
calls.hard_truth: Resolving outstanding claims requires more than acknowledging they exist.

calls.title: Eliminate Indigenous overrepresentation in custody
calls.hard_truth: Reducing Indigenous incarceration requires measurable change in custody rates.

calls.title: Provide alternatives to imprisonment
calls.hard_truth: Alternatives to imprisonment need real availability and community resources.

calls.title: Amend criminal justice policies
calls.hard_truth: Sentencing reforms should be evaluated for actual impacts on Indigenous people.

calls.title: Recognize fetal alcohol spectrum disorder in justice
calls.hard_truth: Justice responses to FASD require accessible assessment and support.

calls.title: Reform justice responses to FASD
calls.hard_truth: Legislative reform should be judged against the specific FASD-related changes the TRC requested.

calls.title: Address Indigenous justice and healing needs
calls.hard_truth: Healing lodges and culturally appropriate services need capacity, not only recognition.

calls.title: Provide culturally relevant correctional services
calls.hard_truth: Correctional programming should be assessed by access and outcomes.

calls.title: Offer support for Indigenous offenders
calls.hard_truth: Community supports after release matter as much as programs inside institutions.

calls.title: Eliminate overrepresentation of Indigenous youth in custody
calls.hard_truth: Reducing Indigenous youth custody requires published results.

calls.title: Publish Indigenous victimization data
calls.hard_truth: Victimization data must be timely and useful to Indigenous communities.

calls.title: Fund Indigenous-specific victim services
calls.hard_truth: Victim services should be culturally appropriate and available, not merely funded on paper.

calls.title: Public inquiry into missing and murdered Indigenous women and girls
calls.hard_truth: A completed national inquiry does not automatically mean its recommendations have been implemented.

calls.title: Commit to Aboriginal justice systems
calls.hard_truth: Recognition of Indigenous justice systems requires concrete jurisdictional and institutional changes.

calls.title: Adopt UNDRIP as reconciliation framework
calls.hard_truth: Adopting UNDRIP in principle is different from fully implementing it in laws and practice.

calls.title: Develop national UNDRIP action plan
calls.hard_truth: An action plan is a roadmap, not proof that its measures have been delivered.

calls.title: Issue Royal Proclamation of Reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: A promised reconciliation proclamation must be judged by whether it is actually issued and implemented.

calls.title: Create Covenant of Reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: A covenant requires meaningful participation and commitments, not just proposed language.

calls.title: Repudiate doctrines of discovery and terra nullius
calls.hard_truth: Rejecting colonial doctrines in statements is different from eliminating their influence in law and policy.

calls.title: Church adoption of UNDRIP
calls.hard_truth: Religious organizations' commitments to UNDRIP must be assessed through their actions.

calls.title: Religious organizations’ compliance with UNDRIP
calls.hard_truth: Public repudiation of harmful doctrines is a step; the broader reconciliation work continues.

calls.title: Establish Indigenous equity in legal systems
calls.hard_truth: Indigenous legal institutions need sustained resources and meaningful authority.

calls.title: Publish legal opinions on Indigenous rights
calls.hard_truth: Transparency about legal positions matters when Indigenous rights are at stake.

calls.title: Respect Indigenous rights in legal doctrine
calls.hard_truth: Legal doctrine can still affect whether Indigenous peoples can exercise recognized rights.

calls.title: Establish a National Council for Reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: Establishing a council is a milestone, not proof that its oversight has all necessary independence and capacity.

calls.title: Provide multi-year funding for the National Council
calls.hard_truth: An oversight body without reliable funding cannot fulfill its mandate effectively.

calls.title: Provide reconciliation data to the National Council
calls.hard_truth: Accountability depends on governments providing the data an oversight body needs.

calls.title: Prime Minister's annual State of Aboriginal Peoples report
calls.hard_truth: An annual public response is different from internal reporting.

calls.title: Educate public servants on Indigenous history and rights
calls.hard_truth: Public-service training needs measurable quality and consequences for practice.

calls.title: Papal apology for residential schools
calls.hard_truth: An apology cannot substitute for every form of repair and reconciliation.

calls.title: Educate congregations on residential schools
calls.hard_truth: Educating congregations is an ongoing responsibility, not a one-time statement.

calls.title: Church training in Indigenous spirituality and history
calls.hard_truth: Training faith leaders should include Indigenous perspectives and lived experience.

calls.title: Church funding for healing and reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: Healing and reconciliation funding should be judged by community priorities and access.

calls.title: Teach residential school history in schools
calls.hard_truth: School curriculum commitments must reach classrooms and teachers.

calls.title: Build Indigenous curriculum and teaching resources
calls.hard_truth: Sharing best practices is not the same as implementing them consistently.

calls.title: Fund reconciliation research
calls.hard_truth: Public funding and protection of Indigenous spiritual practices must match the call's requirements.

calls.title: Support youth reconciliation organizations
calls.hard_truth: Research needs long-term support and Indigenous collaboration.

calls.title: Review museum policies with Indigenous peoples
requirements: Establish multi-year funding for community-based youth organizations delivering reconciliation programs.
Create a national network to share information and best practices.
calls.hard_truth: Youth programs cannot plan long-term work on short-term promises alone.

calls.title: Review museum policies and best practices
calls.hard_truth: Museum policy reform requires Indigenous participation and actual institutional change.

calls.title: Fund Indigenous museum and heritage projects
calls.hard_truth: Commemoration and museum projects should be led or shaped by Indigenous communities.

calls.title: Review archival policies and access
calls.hard_truth: Archives access and repatriation require concrete policies and resources.

calls.title: Fund archival review and reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: Archival reviews should lead to improved access and respectful stewardship.

calls.title: Provide residential school death records
calls.hard_truth: Accurate records matter to families seeking answers about children who never returned home.

calls.title: Create a national residential school death register
calls.hard_truth: A national death register must be complete, responsibly maintained and accessible under appropriate protocols.

calls.title: Create a national residential school burial register
calls.hard_truth: A burial register must respect families and communities while supporting identification and remembrance.

calls.title: Inform families of burial locations
calls.hard_truth: Families deserve timely, respectful information about burial locations.

calls.title: Protect and maintain residential school cemeteries
calls.hard_truth: Site protection requires resources, consultation and sustained stewardship.

calls.title: Develop protocols for burial site work
calls.hard_truth: Work at burial sites must follow Indigenous community protocols and leadership.

calls.title: Provide records to the NCTR
calls.hard_truth: Records cannot contribute to truth if they are withheld from the NCTR.

calls.title: Fund the NCTR
calls.hard_truth: Long-term archival work requires stable institutional funding.

calls.title: Develop a national commemoration framework
calls.hard_truth: A national commemoration framework needs Indigenous participation and implementation.

calls.title: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
calls.hard_truth: A federal statutory holiday is a concrete achievement, but public education cannot be confined to one day.

calls.title: National monument in Ottawa
calls.hard_truth: A national monument must be judged by the specific commitment and its delivery.

calls.title: Residential school monuments in provincial and territorial capitals
calls.hard_truth: Provincial and territorial monuments require jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction accountability.

calls.title: Indigenous and non-Indigenous arts collaboration
calls.hard_truth: Arts collaboration is meaningful when Indigenous creators shape the work.

calls.title: CBC/Radio-Canada reconciliation programming
calls.hard_truth: Broadcast commitments should be assessed by actual Indigenous programming and representation.

calls.title: APTN reconciliation programming
calls.hard_truth: Indigenous broadcasting needs sustained support and reach.

calls.title: Journalism education on Indigenous history
calls.hard_truth: Journalism education is essential because inaccurate coverage can perpetuate harm.

calls.title: Indigenous athletes in sports history
calls.hard_truth: Sports history must recognize Indigenous athletes and their contributions.

calls.title: Support North American Indigenous Games
calls.hard_truth: Games funding should be reliable enough to sustain Indigenous participation.

calls.title: Make federal sport legislation inclusive
calls.hard_truth: Inclusive sports legislation requires more than aspirational language.

calls.title: Inclusive national sports programs
calls.hard_truth: Sports policy should be measured by access and Indigenous representation.

calls.title: Respect Indigenous protocols at sporting events
calls.hard_truth: Respecting Indigenous protocols at sporting events requires practice, not symbolism alone.

calls.title: Business adoption of UNDRIP
requirements: Adopt UNDRIP as a reconciliation framework.
Commit to meaningful consultation and free, prior and informed consent before economic development projects.
Ensure equitable Indigenous access to jobs, training and education.
Provide staff training on Indigenous history, rights and anti-racism.
calls.hard_truth: A corporate reconciliation statement is not proof of consent, equitable opportunity or staff training.

calls.title: Teach newcomers Indigenous history
calls.responsible: Federal government and national Indigenous organizations
requirements: Revise newcomer information and citizenship tests to include Treaties, residential schools and Indigenous histories.
calls.hard_truth: Newcomer education should accurately include Treaties and residential-school history.

calls.title: Include Treaties in citizenship oath
requirements: Revise the Oath of Citizenship to include a commitment to faithfully observe Treaties with Indigenous Peoples.
calls.hard_truth: Changing the citizenship oath is a specific legislative achievement; learning and understanding still matter.
